summary.text:
The task is to judge the exact BOOK ENTRY for "Dew" against the strongest specific alternative, using the chapter as evidence.
The book entry's core claim—that dew in these texts symbolizes the Word of God descending silently from heaven, like manna on the ground, and evaporating without root—fits the supplied evidence more tightly than the common reading of divine blessing or grace.

The primary basis in the entry (Deut 32:2, 8:3, Num 11:9, Ex 16:14) directly ties the “speech shall distil as the dew” to the manna narrative, where dew is the silent nightly moisture that appears in the morning and nourishes the daily bread. The entry then layers the sower parable’s mechanics ( Deut 8:3 links manna to “every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the LORD”; the evaporation motif matches the seed on stony ground that withers when the sun rises). Hosea 14:5 and Isaiah 26:19 are used to show the same figure applied to life-giving or resurrection power, while 1 Kings 17:1 shows the withholding of dew as judgment on the word. This single referent— the Word—explains the entire cluster without contradiction.

The strongest counter-reading treats dew as primarily divine blessing, favor, or refreshment (the consensus in the glossary responses). That view accounts for Genesis 27:28, Deuteronomy 33, Hosea 14:5, Psalm 133:3, and Zechariah 8:12 as life-giving moisture in the arid climate. But it leaves the manna-dew link (Num 11:9, Ex 16:14) as incidental provision rather than the explicit “word lies on the ground as daily bread” the entry derives, and it treats Deuteronomy 32:2’s “my speech shall distil as the dew” as merely one secondary simile instead of the defining image. The counter therefore requires more steps to explain why the entry’s chosen texts 32:2, 8:3, 11:9, and 16:14 are grouped together, and why the evaporation motif is highlighted.

The entry’s identification therefore accounts for the exact scriptural references printed with it, the mechanics of silent nightly arrival and morning appearance, and the manna-to-word transition with fewer unsupported assertions. The blessing reading is broader and more common, but it does not explain the specific textual connections the glossary entry is asked to illuminate. The book entry is the better-supported explanation. 

PERSUADED, FULL.

support_scope.description: Support for the exact glossary BOOK ENTRY only, never for the supporting chapter as a whole.

book_secondary_elaborations.description: Secondary assertions actually printed in the glossary BOOK ENTRY; exclude chapter-only claims.

unsupported_glossary_assertions.description: Material assertions actually printed in the BOOK ENTRY that the evidence does not support. Must be empty for FULL and nonempty for CORE_ONLY.

chapter_only_objections.description: Objections to applications or arguments found only in the supporting chapter. Preserved for later chapter review and excluded from the glossary scope ruling.
